blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Describing landscapes from photographs and images, adding geographical detail to maps, and using supporting material together with a map extract.

blocks.heading: Describing a photograph
blocks.text: A photograph is described from what it shows, organised from the foreground through the middle distance to the background, with the position words doing the organising. In the foreground, a flat field system with rectangular plots; in the middle distance, a steep slope under grass with a track climbing it; in the background, a flat-topped ridge against the sky. The description names landforms, vegetation, land use and buildings, with suitable geographical terms and simple adjectives. It adds nothing the photograph does not show, and it explains nothing either: features that cannot be pointed to in the image are invented, and reasons are explanation, which a describe question has not asked for.

blocks.heading: Adding detail to a map
blocks.text: Applying knowledge to a map means adding what the symbols imply. A weir on the river means a head of water, and a mill beside it means the head was used. Contours bending upstream in a V mark the valley the river has cut, so the flow direction is read off the Vs. Land use follows the relief, so the flat ground by the stream is the settlement's best land, and the inference is tied to the evidence on the sheet: each added detail names the symbol it comes from.

blocks.heading: Using material together
blocks.text: A map and a photograph read together let one source check the other: the photograph shows what the contour pattern means on the ground, and the map places what the photograph shows. A valley that looks broad in the image is measured on the map; a slope that looks steep on the sheet is checked against the photograph's horizon. Aerial photographs and satellite images extend the same skill, and a GIS layer, a data theme drawn over the base map, joins a distribution to the ground it lies on.

blocks.heading: Where this connects
blocks.text: The photographs described here show the landforms of topics 2.2 and 2.3, and the map skills they sit with are the ones of the first two units of this topic.
